the_one_metric: The full-year 2026 adjusted guidance raise and book-to-bill - orders $1.1B, +8%, a 1.16x book-to-bill and record defence-electronics demand are what this print trades on, not the $3.72 adjusted EPS
whats_priced_in: A good quarter was already being bought: +10.16% over the five sessions into the event, 5.6% off the 52w high, and a 6.99x forward P/S that is the richest in its aerospace-defence peer set.
bear_case: The raise is small in dollar terms - FY EPS midpoint moves only from $15.10 to $15.25 - Defence Electronics sales fell 3% y/y, and reported +5% sales against an 8-9% FY guide implies a steep H2 that a 10% pre-print run has already paid for.
key_drivers: Q2 press release in-corpus: sales $924M +5%, adjusted EPS $3.72 +15%, adjusted operating margin 19.4% (+110bps), all three segments expanding margin
FY 2026 guidance raised on every line - sales to 8-9%, operating income to 11-13%, EPS to $15.10-$15.40, FCF to $585-605M
Orders $1.1B +8%, book-to-bill 1.16x, backlog $4.5B +10% since December, record defence-electronics demand
Offsetting: +10.16% 5-day run-up into the print and a Defence Electronics segment down 3% on revenue
what_would_change_my_mind: Segment guidance or call commentary flagging that the H2 acceleration implied by the 8-9% FY sales range depends on shipment timing rather than backlog conversion.
reasoning: The corpus contains the actual Q2 release, timestamped after the 08-05 close and therefore inside the measurement window: a clean beat with a raise across sales, margin, EPS and FCF, and a 1.16x book-to-bill on record defence-electronics orders. CW's eight-event mean absolute reaction is 3.98%; I expect a normal-sized up move, not a gap.
